explanation: Five years on sale and declining year on year: about 2,805 a month this spring against 3,643 a year ago. Tagged for Halloween, it peaks in August and again in October, so the models (15,197 to 23,473) give 17,606 (5,325 in October), well below last year's 40,794. Adjusted +1.8% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 17,919.

Three years on sale; about 2,716 a month this spring against 5,220 a year ago, and June fell to 2,013. The models agree (14,189 to 17,865) on 15,328, with the August peak for jeans, against 35,695 last year. Adjusted +2.3% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 15,684.

Three years on sale and still rising: 3,782 units in April, 5,200 in June. Last year it sold 22,698 in July-October from a slightly lower spring rate; the models agree closely (24,964 to 34,255) and give 30,147, with the August back-to-school peak for jeans. Adjusted +1.8% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 30,677; confidence 1.

A summer short two years on sale, steady at about 2,958 a month, half its rate of a year ago (6,005). The models agree (6,889 to 11,567) on 9,634: July and August a little above the current rate, then the usual drop after summer. Adjusted +1.6% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 9,787; confidence 1.

Out of stock: no sales since 10 April. Forecast as if back in stock, as the brief asks: its January-March rate (about 32 a month) x the seasonal pattern of tops at least a year old. No model covers it, so the number is a rule; confidence 3.

Steady at about 3,826 a month all spring. Last year it sold 34,393 in July-October from the same rate; the models (19,983 to 29,441) expect a smaller autumn step for an item now two years old and give 20,895, with October, its Halloween month, the highest. Adjusted +1.4% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 21,196; if last year's step repeats, it will come in higher.

A bikini top tagged for the 4th of July, on sale since February; June was its best month (1,952 units). The holiday passes early in July and swimwear falls after it, so the models (2,794 to 7,626) give 3,861: 1,803 in July, 408 by October. Adjusted +1.5% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 3,919; if the June rise was mostly holiday demand, July will come in lower.

A hoodie launched last summer; spring sales fell from 2,880 in April to 1,678 in June, as hoodies do. It sold 15,156 in July-October last year; the models give 16,175, rising to 4,827 in October. Adjusted +1.6% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 16,430; their wide range (11,961 to 28,436) is the doubt about a second autumn as strong as its first.

A graduation dress: sales peaked in May (5,820 units) and fell to 1,376 in June once the season ended, with the last June week under 200. The models (5,433 to 12,499) give 7,435, about half the spring rate. Adjusted +1.1% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 7,518; with graduation over, the late-June pace points lower: the clearest downside risk among the larger items.

About a year on sale; June dipped to 972 after 2,160 in May. It sold 7,161 in July-October last year, in its launch season; the models split (4,732 to 13,273) and their average gives 8,308. Adjusted +1.1% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 8,399; one of the widest model ranges among the larger items.

A sweater launched last autumn; spring sales fell to 830 in June, as expected. Sweaters climb from August, so the models' forecast rises to 3,446 in October, 10,544 in total. Adjusted +1.5% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 10,704; the models range widely (7,306 to 20,450) on how strong its second autumn will be.

Small in spring (about 362 a month), but June more than doubled to 580. It sells with the sweaters, so the models (4,332 to 6,393) give 4,996, more than three times the recent rate, on the autumn season and its June momentum. Adjusted +1.0% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 5,044.

On sale since February and in volume since April, at about 2,497 a month. The models range 7,222 to 14,888 and give 8,946: a little above the spring rate in July and August, then 1,415 in October, including a 13% lift from the launch-weighted tree. Adjusted +1.4% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 9,074.

Launched 30 April and already the largest item: 7,711 units in June, with weekly sales peaking in mid-June. The six models range 22,460 to 42,558 and give 33,490 (July above June, then fading), including a 14% lift from the launch-weighted tree. Adjusted +2.2% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 34,243; the last June week was below the peak, so it is the first item to re-forecast.

Launched 12 April; 4,687 units in June at a steady 1,000-1,300 a week. The models range 14,047 to 23,427 and give 17,814 (6,596 in July, down to 2,583 by October), including a 9% lift from the launch-weighted tree. Adjusted +1.4% for the two new site sales (August, September), to 18,071.

World Cup and 4th of July tee launched 25 May; 6,685 units in June, about 306 a day in late June. The models answer 35,457 (P10-P90 14,616-65,984), not knowing the tournament ends on 19 July. I set July to the late-June pace until the final and capped Aug-Oct at 75/50/45% of July, the post-event decay of past holiday items. Final 23,096. Confidence 3: one season, event-driven demand.

World Cup shorts launched 25 May, flat at about 30 a day in June (928 units). The models answer 4,984 (P10-P90 2,787-7,773), not knowing the tournament ends on 19 July. I set July to the late-June pace until the final and capped Aug-Oct at 75/50/45% of July, the post-event decay of past holiday items. Final 2,279. Confidence 3: one season, event-driven demand.
